subject: Dedicated capacity queued slowdown and shortfall — mitigation & follow-up
messages:

Date: 2028-07-30T16:12:00Z
Subject: Major latency + 429s on dedicated pool (NimbleAI-prod)

Hi Sofia,

We're seeing a sharp increase in token latency and a lot of 429s against our dedicated pool (NimbleAI-prod) starting ~08:50 PDT. Median latencies jumped from ~120ms to >1s and tail is much higher. This is affecting our interactive application.

Attached are the client-side traces and a small sample of failed requests (client_logs.json). Can you confirm whether this is on your side or if there's anything we need to change from our end?

This is high priority for us — please escalate.

I'll follow up with timeboxed updates every 30–60 minutes and share our remediation plan + postmortem commitment.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T17:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: initial triage — pool scheduler contended, eviction thrash observed

Logging what I found after a quick pass:
- Symptoms: sustained queue depth on the dedicated GPU pool servicing NimbleAI-prod, an increase in GPU memory retention time and repeated preemptive evictions (eviction rate x3 vs baseline).
- Probable immediate cause: a scheduled kernel/runtime update earlier this morning (internal deploy at 06:30 PDT) changed memory reuse heuristics and exposed an aggressive tenant eviction policy we configured to enforce headroom. The combination caused longer-lived allocations and increased queuing.

Immediate remediation executed (10:50–11:00 PDT):
1) Disabled tenant-level preemptive eviction for NimbleAI-prod (removed aggressive headroom enforcement).
2) Shifted 20% of incoming requests to a fallback variant (redwood-small) via runtime traffic split.
3) Forced KV cache warm-up for top prefixes we saw in the logs to reduce token generation cost.
4) Scaled dedicated pool by adding two warm-standby nodes from the reserved pool (short-term allocation).

I've attached a quick snapshot of queue lengths and contention (pool-queues-07030.svg). We'll monitor for normalization. Longer-term action items we need to track in the postmortem:
- Revert or patch the kernel/runtime change with a regression test for eviction behavior.
- Introduce a gradual rollout gate for memory allocation heuristics.
- Hard SLO for eviction rate per-tenant.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-07-30T18:40:00Z
Subject: Status update: traffic split live; latency improving

Quick operational update for the thread: 
- At 11:02 PDT we applied an 80/20 traffic split (80% -> primary model, 20% -> redwood-small).
- KV cache warming completed for the top 12 prefixes at 11:18 PDT.
- Observed median latency drop from ~1.1s -> ~420ms over 25 minutes; 95th tail reduced by ~45%.
- We have the two reserve nodes online and routing; queue depth for NimbleAI-prod reduced by ~60%.

Continuing monitoring for next 24 hours. If we see re-escalation we'll revert traffic split and move to faster capacity refresh.

Grace
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-31T20:45:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: timeline, credits, and postmortem plan for 2028-07-30 incident

Hi Caroline — thank you again for the patience and quick confirmation. Summary and next steps below: 

What happened (short): 
- A runtime kernel change combined with an aggressive tenant eviction setting produced longer-lived GPU allocations and queue growth for your dedicated pool. That caused higher latencies and rate limiting responses for a subset of requests between 08:50–11:20 PDT.

What we did (actions): 
- Immediate: traffic split to fallback model, disabled tenant preemptive eviction, warmed KV caches, added two warm-standby nodes.
- Short-term: blocked the kernel rollout and drafted a targeted patch for memory reuse heuristics.
- Long-term: implementing a rollout gate + eviction-rate SLO + automated warm-standby reservation for at-risk tenants.

Customer impact and credit: 
- We logged the incident under DL-83921. We'll issue a one-time credit equal to 72 hours of Dedicated runtime charges for NimbleAI-prod; Vanesssa will follow up with billing details and a HubSpot record.

Next steps and timeline: 
- Postmortem doc: shared doc link (internal editable) by EOD 2028-07-31: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-incident-brief
- Live postmortem review (technical + CS): scheduled 2028-07-31 16:00 PDT — meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/sofia/nimbleai-postmortem-2028-07-31
- Engineering patch rollout targeted 2028-08-03 (will be gate-kept by gradual traffic ramp).

Action owners: 
- Karthik: root cause write-up + patch PR and rollout gating (ETA 2028-08-02)
- Grace: post-incident monitoring dashboard and eviction-rate SLO (ETA 2028-08-01)
- Vanessa: billing credit ops and HubSpot update (ETA 2028-07-31)
- Priyom: follow-up tests with NimbleAI test harness for traffic patterns (ETA 2028-08-02)

If you'd like a private sync earlier than the scheduled postmortem, I can set it up — otherwise we'll present the full RCA in the review and share the incident-brief.pdf after that meeting.

Sincerely,
Sofia Ivanova
